trigger: Submit the arrival immediately after every anchor's first streamed token. Preserve client timing and observed engine groups. Require at least one actual mixed forward in every candidate sample; a missed overlap fails eligibility, not a removable timing outlier.
metric: Mean completion time of the anchor requests, measured from each HTTP submission. Arrival completion, TTFT and delivery gaps are protected and reported separately.
confirmation: Repeat the complete ABBA comparison in an independent process. Preserve all samples, outputs and quality outcomes. These remain small workload-specific experiments; no tail-percentile or universal speed claim.

gates.quality: All automatic checks and explicit rubric review pass. Never compare speed on failed quality. Natural EOS, existing sampling and output budgets remain unchanged.
gates.correctness: Separate-target oracle for per-request state/KV/features and sampled laws; untouched slots and cache loans; every accepted/EOS/budget position; failure poisoning and full resource recovery. Numerical shape changes require the existing parity criteria, never silent tolerance relaxation.
gates.protection: Full local-v1 manifest, including decode-only, long/reused contexts, sampling, cancellation and small budgets. Candidate and control retain equal optional workspace allocation during timing.
gates.ablation: Measure mlp-only and scheduled separate target forwards independently to distinguish projection sharing from changed scheduling. Defaults remain off.
